difftest/extract_upstream.py copies these files (whole, up to their test module) or items verbatim from the commit into difftest/src/upstream/ under their upstream module paths, so they compile unchanged. The copied code runs on real axum requests through axum::middleware::from_fn_with_state. difftest/sqlx-mock is a stand-in for sqlx: each SQL statement upstream sends is evaluated by hand in difftest/src/shell.rs over the kernel's snapshot (WHERE, JOIN, EXISTS, scalar subqueries, NULL, Postgres inet <<=). create_permission itself takes axum state, so its gate sequence is transcribed in tests.rs; the gates it calls are the copied ones.

Not covered (trusted input)

difftest/extract_upstream.py builds difftest/upstream, a crate named kanidmd_lib laid out like server/lib/src. The six files of the access module other than mod.rs and profiles.rs are copied whole; from those two, and from entry.rs, filter.rs, value.rs, valueset/*.rs, modify.rs, event.rs, server/identity.rs, server/batch_modify.rs, constants/{entries,uuids}.rs and macros.rs, the items the module uses are cut by name, so crate:: paths resolve unchanged. kanidm_proto's attribute.rs and constants.rs are copied into upstream/proto (without the OpenAPI derive, which is not available offline). Stubs (upstream/stubs/) stand in for the entry states, the ValueSetT trait object, the filter cache and the logging macros (no-ops). Seams appended after the copied text build profiles, entries, filters and modify lists and implement AccessControlsTransaction over given profiles.

src/tests.rs runs all seven public operations of the trait on both sides for 100,000 random cases (profiles with group, entry-manager and empty receivers and random target filters, user, sync and internal identities with every access scope, entries with protected, sync, OAuth2, application and migration classes, modify lists, batch modify sets, created entries) and compares released entries, reduced attribute sets, effective permissions and decisions.   • The transaction machinery (CowCell, ARCache), SCIM conversions, logs.
  • Value syntaxes other than utf8, iutf8, iname, uuid, reference, uint32 and OAuth2 scope maps.

Hand-written stubs supply the rest: ruma's ids, event types and request/response structs; the error type and its macros; a Pdu with the Event accessors; the implement macro; and an in-memory database whose columns are ordered byte maps with upstream's key encoding (RawPduId bytes, 0xFF-separated tuples, big-endian counts), so the copied scans (raw_stream_from, rev_raw_keys_from, ...) read the same rows in the same order as on RocksDB. The short and state_compressor lookups are transcribed.

tests.rs builds random rooms by appending events the way the append path does (state before each event, current state, the state cache as update_membership leaves it, relation and thread indexes), perturbs some, and compares the kernel's reply with the copied route's on 240,000 requests; it also asserts that ten subtle paths are taken (interleaved /relations recursion, the backward /messages token at stream end, to bounds, departed users in initialSync, ...). Seven kernel mutations (a <= to < in user_shared_history, the from bound of pdus, the queue order of the /relations recursion, once_joined to is_left in user_can_see_state_events, the thread token bound, the backward to bound, the server allow list) each fail it.

props.rs checks each statement of proofs/Properties.lean on random inputs, with its premises holding at least 300 times.

Not covered (trusted input)

  • Parsing: tokens arrive as Token::{Absent, At(count), Invalid}; ids are numbers. The server of user u is u / 1000.
  • Lazy loading of members is off (/messages returns no state, /context the full state). Presentation is not modeled: unsigned (age, transaction ids, MSC4115 membership), bundled aggregations, the MSC3856 ignored-thread view, event formats.
  • Federation is off: no backfill, no remote fetch of a missing /context event.
  • Writes: upstream's live_thread deletes stale thread activity rows while reading; one request runs per snapshot, so the kernel ignores the delete.
  • /event with include_unredacted_content (power levels) is not ported.
  • Not ported: sync v3/v5, search, /timestamp_to_event, room summary, redaction and invite authorization (user_can_redact, user_can_invite), state resolution and the append path.

tasks.property: Every non-admin turned away by admin_middleware is audited, and nothing else is written.
admin_middleware passes only an admin whose credential carries the admin or * scope, or no scope ceiling.
An anonymous request reaches a non-public repository only through an anonymous read rule that applies to the client IP.
A PUT, PATCH or DELETE reaches a format handler only with a principal, never on a download ticket.
A stored anonymous rule grants only read, on a repository or project, under the nil principal id.
CidrRange::contains is agreement on the first prefix_len bits.
With guest access off, a request with no credential gets through only on an allowlisted path.
A non-admin write outside the negotiation routes goes through only if the repository-action rule grants it.
Only an admin creates a permission rule.
A non-admin principal reaches a private repository only if it holds a role assignment or an applicable rule on it.
check_repository_action computes its SQL: admin role wins, else applicable rules decide, else roles.
An applicable rule without the action denies, whatever the principal's non-admin roles grant.
A repository-restricted credential reaches a repository outside its allowlist only to read a public one.
scopes_grant_access computes the reference model scopeGrants.
A download ticket is consumed only by a GET or HEAD, and only if it is live.
A download ticket authorizes only GET or HEAD, as a non-admin principal with no scopes.
The repository visibility middleware never panics, overflows or diverges.
The account-request identity creates only sign-up requests with their six attributes.
The anonymous user reads only what search profiles grant; the OAuth2 and application rules give it nothing.
A user creates an entry only through a create profile with a group receiver covering the user, a target matching the entry, and every attribute and class of the entry allowed.
Users and migrations never create builtin entries or entries of a protected class.
A user deletes an entry only through a delete profile whose receiver covers the user and whose target matches the entry.
Users and migrations never delete builtin entries or entries of a protected class.
When the protection rules deny creating an entry, no create profile can allow it.
When the protection rules deny a modification of an entry, no modify profile can allow it.
The effective-permission report never panics, overflows or loops.
An equality filter term matches exactly when the entry's value set for the attribute holds the value.
A user modification sets an attribute only where an applicable modify profile allows it.
Only the internal system identity adds a protected class to an entry.
A user session that is not read-write modifies nothing.
Every attribute a search returns is granted on that entry by an applicable search profile, or is one of the few attributes the OAuth2, application and sync-account rules release.
The substring test used by filter terms is List.IsInfix.
On an unprotected entry owned by a sync agreement, a user sets only the session attributes and those the agreement yields; without a single sync parent nothing changes.
A sync agreement, or a user session scoped to synchronisation, sees no entries.
Only the internal system identity modifies a tombstone.
With authentication enabled, a request to an admin path reaches its handler only with the admin role.
In audit mode a namespace mismatch never denies a request.
The Docker catalog and the token pages are never served without credentials.
The trusted-proxy check compares the top prefix bits of the address.
validate_digest accepts exactly sha256 and sha512 digests.
An accepted Docker name has the OCI shape.
A failed attempt is recorded only when the presented credentials were wrong.
The failure count is cleared only when the presented credentials were right.
The subject glob matcher computes the reference model `globSpec`.
A token whose lifetime exceeds the provider's ceiling is refused.
A client locked out by the failure tracker authenticates only on open paths.
The authentication middleware never panics or diverges while no failure counter is at u32::MAX.
A request without credentials never reaches a handler with a role that can write.
An enforced write to a namespace goes through only if the namespace is inside the provider scope, unless that scope contains `*`.
A write goes through only if the first role rule matching the token's subject grants write or admin.
An accepted Docker reference is a digest or a tag.
A revoked API token is refused afterwards, also when it was cached.
Once revoke_all_for_user removed a token of a user, no token authenticates as that user.
An enforced write goes through only if the namespace is also inside the matched rule's scope.
The backtracking segment matcher agrees with the plain recursive glob `segGlobSpec`.
An accepted storage key cannot leave its directory.
An API token is accepted only with the nra_ prefix and while a cached or stored record for it has not expired.
The authorization kernel never panics, overflows or diverges.
Forwarding headers from a peer outside the trusted proxies are ignored.
A write method on a gated path, other than the npm audit endpoints, reaches its handler only with a role that can write.
The permission check always answers.
Creating a grant needs Share on the resource.
On a read-only drive nothing inside it, nor the drive, can be changed.
Expired grants play no part in an access decision.
Taking grants away never allows more.
Creating a grant or setting a role never leaves a drive that had an owner without one.
In storage-migration read-only mode only reads are allowed.
A personal drive's membership cannot be changed by creating a grant or setting a role.
A refused grant creation or role change writes nothing.
Share permission is granted only through a live Owner grant.
A grant created on a folder or file obeys its drive's sharing and public-link policies.
A link token is allowed only through a live grant to that token.
Unless the caller owns the resource or only denials are checked, an allowed request has an Allow statement that applies.
A bucket policy allows a non-owner only through an Allow statement whose principal matches the account.
Bucket policy evaluation always terminates without a panic.
A cleaned path has no empty or dot segments.
Cleaning a path twice gives the same result as cleaning it once.
With deny_only, a request no Deny statement refuses is allowed.
An explicit Deny that applies refuses the request, whatever the policy allows.
Force-delete is granted only by an Allow statement that names it; s3:* never grants it.
A statement naming s3:GetObjectVersion also covers s3:GetObject.
An Allow statement with only NotAction never covers a force-delete.
The owner is allowed unless a Deny statement applies.
The condition parser reads integers as str::parse::<i64> does.
Policy variable resolution terminates when no substituted value contains a variable reference.
The wildcard matcher computes the declarative glob.
The events /context returns before and after the base event are the first /messages pages backward and forward from it.
Any base event /context serves is also served by /event.
Under joined or invited history visibility, the events /context returns satisfy the Matrix spec's visibility rule.
/context returns the requested base event and surrounding events, all in the room and visible to the user.
A user whose current membership is a leave or ban gets no event after their departure from initialSync.
initialSync returns only events of the room the user may see.
/joined_members needs the user to be joined or the room to be world-readable.
A user whose last membership event is a leave or ban gets no event sent after it from /messages unless that event is world-readable.
/messages pages in count order within the from and to tokens and returns at most limit (capped at 1000) events.
/messages returns only events of the room that the user may see under tuwunel's history-visibility rule and has not ignored.
/relations needs readable room state and returns only events of the room the user may see.
/event returns the requested event, and only if the visibility rule allows it for the room in the path.
Over federation, a joined-visibility event is shown to a server only if one of its users, joined now, was joined at the event.
Reading room state or members needs the user to be joined, invited, once joined, or the room to be world-readable.
/threads returns only thread roots of the room the user may see.
Every request gets a reply: the kernel neither panics nor loops.
An event that was world-readable when sent is served by /event to anyone who has not ignored its sender.
